title: Magnetic and Magnetocaloric Properties of an Eight-Spin Ring Molecular Magnet: Analytical Investigation and Monte-Carlo Simulation
content: We investigated the magnetic and magnetocaloric properties of cyclic (M8) single-molecule magnets (SMMs) composed of eight M3+ ions, where M represents either V or Cr, possessing integer spin-1 or half-integer spin-3/2, respectively. The spins within each molecule are interconnected via an isotropic exchange coupling, J, which may be ferro- or antiferromagnetic for M = Cr, and predominantly antiferromagnetic for M = V. Employing two complementary methodologies, the analytic exact diagonalisation of the Heisenberg spin Hamiltonian and Monte Carlo simulations (MCS), we explored coupling regimes. In the first regime, antiferromagnetic exchange couplings among the spins of single-molecule magnets (SMMs) gave rise to several exotic phenomena, including step-like magnetization plateaus, low-temperature magnetic anisotropy, and quantum phase transitions. In the second regime characterized by ferromagnetic couplings in the V8 system, the spin structure reaches complete saturation, forming a giant pseudo-spin S = 8 ground state. Additionally, conventional magnetic cooling effects (MCE) and inverse magnetic cooling effects (IMCE) were observed. Both analytical and numerical techniques provide complementary advantages for characterizing such molecular magnetic systems. This study paves the way for novel nanotechnology devices based on magnetic nanoparticles and the design of efficient molecular magnetic refrigerants.
